articles.title: ‘Online sex workers literally have to bare it all’: why Patricia Nilsson is exposing the world’s biggest porn bosses
articles.summary: As a business journalist, Nilsson began rigorously reporting on the power players of the adult industry, who prefer to remain in the shadows. Along the way, she uncovered how porn has shaped the internet – and our lives as a whole.
body: There was a time, a few decades ago, when the men who owned the world’s biggest pornography businesses were happy to be famous. They paraded a lifestyle they hoped looked glamorous, appearing in public dressed in silk pyjamas or with a woman in swimwear on each arm. Porn moguls like Hustler’s Larry Flynt or Playboy’s Hugh Hefner were household names.

“Say what you want about these old perverts, who once set the tone of our sexual culture, but at least you knew who they were and what they were selling,” Patricia Nilsson writes in her new book, Guilty Pleasure: The Pornification of the Internet, the Economy, and Everything Else. “These days, the men calling the shots are nowhere to be seen.”

It’s not that they simply feel shy about posing alongside the women who generate their income, or are wary of giving interviews. The owners of the industry’s biggest companies are so anxious to remain anonymous that we often don’t even know their names. They have understood that it is wiser to live in total obscurity.
points: As a business journalist, Nilsson began rigorously reporting on the power players of the adult industry, who prefer to remain in the shadows.
Along the way, she uncovered how porn has shaped the internet – and our lives as a whole.

articles.title: Houseplant hacks: should you water plants less in winter?
articles.summary: Don’t water based on the month or the season – be led by what the plant is actually doing. The problem Cutting back on watering for winter has become so ingrained that people start rationing by the calendar, giving plants just a fraction of the water they had in summer, because the season changed.
body: The hack The advice to reduce is because, as light levels drop, most houseplants slow their growth, use less water and dry out more slowly, so watering as you did in summer risks waterlogging the roots and causing rot.
The method When we get to October, reduce watering to half or a quarter of what you gave plants in the summer.

The test I reduced watering in two of my own plants last winter. A calathea in a cooler, dimmer room dried out more slowly and needed less watering, exactly as the hack predicts. But a pothos sitting under a grow light in a warm room kept growing and started crisping at the edges and dropping yellow leaves.

The verdict The winter watering rule is not a myth, but it is badly misunderstood. The key is to water according to what the plant is doing, not what the calendar says. Research your plant to see if it has a dormant season and check each plant before you water. Push a finger a couple of inches into the compost, or lift the pot to feel its weight – a bone-dry pot is light, a wet one is heavy.
points: Don’t water based on the month or the season – be led by what the plant is actually doing.

articles.title: Saunas, cinnamon buns and coastal scenery on the new rail route from Malmö to Oslo
articles.summary: A new direct train service connects the far south of Sweden to the Norwegian capital in just over six hours, with the option of stopping off in the seaside town of Varberg or lively Gothenburg en route. ‘This carriage is due for modernisation.
body: ‘T his carriage is due for modernisation. Don’t miss the opportunity to experience 90s Germany style,” reads the sign on the door to the dining carriage. The couple inside aren’t missing theirs: they’re taking endless selfies in the clinical pink-and-turquoise carriage that looks like a hospital canteen and smells like cinnamon buns and strong filter coffee.

I’m on Snälltåget’s iconic red-shelled train, on the Swedish rail company’s new route from Malmö to Oslo – a 6.5-hour journey along Sweden’s picturesque western corridor. Until now, the journey between the two cities involved long bus rides and fragmented train transfers. This direct line is easier and cheaper, with tickets starting at £11 each way. It’s already a hit, shuttling more than 25,000 passengers since launching this summer.

I was first seduced by Scandi rail travel a decade ago on a journey from Stockholm to Gothenburg, when I was berthed in a cosy dark-wood cabin and listened to a pianist play in a dining car. This time, starting in Malmö, I will take advantage of the new route to make a series of stops along the country’s western shore.

articles.title: The pest I’ll never forget: I turned the toaster upside down. A mouse fell out
articles.summary: We tried humane traps, wire wool, hardcore cleaning regimes. Nothing worked. In the end, I wondered if the mice in our house were the real residents, while we were the intruders. Some of the happiest years of my 20s were spent in a house-share in east London.
body: We were also not particularly clean, which meant our cluttered, chaotic house was the ideal home for mice. At first we told ourselves it was just one mouse we saw running along next to the skirting board or darting behind a sofa. But a quick scan of the internet confirmed our fears that it’s never just one – mice are social creatures, and they were likely in a nest-share similar to our house-share. A female mouse gives birth to a litter of five to eight mice and can be pregnant up to 10 times a year. We read forum posts that claimed mice were doubly incontinent (something I’ve since learned is fake news), and our horror began to grow.

As the sightings increased and droppings appeared on the kitchen worktop, we agreed something had to be done. Two of my housemates were vegetarian, so we laid humane traps, with a plan to set the creatures free in the garden or a park. The humane traps did not work. The mice continued to thrive and multiply.
points: We tried humane traps, wire wool, hardcore cleaning regimes.
In the end, I wondered if the mice in our house were the real residents, while we were the intruders.

articles.title: Min Jin Lee on Her New Novel, ‘American Hagwon’
articles.summary: With 2007’s “Free Food For Millionaires,” 2015’s National Book Award finalist “Pachinko,” and “American Hagwon,” out today, Lee has worked steadily on what she’s called the “Diaspora Quartet.” She spoke to Vogue about near-death experience, writerly advice, and Thom Browne.
body: There are some authors who plumb the roots of their own concerns or anxieties, while others work tirelessly to build worlds out of words and ideas. Of equal effort but requiring far more generosity is the work Min Jin Lee has been doing for over 30 years, telling stories about the integrity of the human spirit that span time and continents. Another aspect of Lee’s work—and a hallmark of any conversation with her—is its warmth, curiosity, and thoughtfulness. She has a way of reminding you that the world, however difficult, is full of possibility.

Min Jin Lee: Hagwons are everywhere in Korea and I visited them here too. Some call them “cram schools,” but that’s not quite right. They are places of learning, where you can pursue knowledge of anything, really.
In the case of this book, it seems like they teach you how to live.

Early on, you introduce Mido, an incredible and misunderstood young woman. Two points stood out for me. “The world was too noisy” and “Mido was able to pick up from observation whatever she needed to know.” Is the world too noisy? And, as a result, is the world less perceptive?
points: With 2007’s “Free Food For Millionaires,” 2015’s National Book Award finalist “Pachinko,” and “American Hagwon,” out today, Lee has worked steadily on what she’s called the “Diaspora Quartet.

articles.title: The 17 Best Airbnbs in Oaxaca Have Plenty of Rustic Appeal
articles.summary: For an alternative to Mexico City, stay in one of the best Airbnbs in Oaxaca—from cozy studios to open-air villas, these are the best places to book.
body: Our top picks are scattered throughout the region; we found cozy studios and sprawling villas alike, depending on your plans and the size of your travel party. One thing unites these properties: Between Brutalist spaces drenched in color and apartments that put local craft front and center, each of these 17 vacation rentals is brimming with design inspiration. Find the right Oaxacan Airbnb stay for you, below.

Described as “an island in the heart of the city,” this one-bedroom apartment sits inside a traditional Oaxacan house in the historic city center, where the rooms wrap around a patio, shaded by an avocado tree. The home features modern interiors filled with handmade objects, organic materials, and assorted homeware from local artisans. The unit has its own entrance, a small private front patio, a full kitchen, and a compact workspace. In the bedroom, you’ll find an open shower that looks onto a small interior garden. Start each morning at the bakery and café located at the home’s street level, which many locals credit with some of the best bread in Oaxaca.

articles.summary: Vogue Business brings you a weekly update of the most interesting stories in the world of AI that you need on your radar.Stay tuned as we spotlight AI initiatives in the fashion and beauty industry each week.
body: The Vogue Business AI Tracker keeps a record of the most important AI developments that will influence our industry and our world, each week. From venture capital investments and startup launches to product drops and regulatory updates, we’ll make sure you never miss a beat when it comes to the AI news that matters.
The news: Meta unveils kawaii-coded wearable pendant to house its Muse AI assistant.

Why it matters: Just when we thought Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg had finished announcing his slew of smart glasses and AI updates during the annual connect conference, there was “just one more thing”: another wearable device designed to house its new Muse AI agent, the Muse Charm. It’s a tamagotchi-esque, palm-sized totem on a looped cord designed to attach to keychains or fit into the wearer’s pocket.

The Muse Charm has a small screen to display the user’s selected Muse AI avatar. It’s unlocked via fingerprint and can be spoken into for instructing their agent to carry out tasks. Zuckerberg is still “finalizing” the components, but promised that the device will be ready to ship before the holidays.

articles.title: Rocky Mountain High: Hiking With Moncler Grenoble and Aspen’s Legendary Hotel Jerome
articles.summary: A new partnership between Aspen's premier hotel and the high-performance alpine-wear brand is a perfect meeting of the minds (at 8,000 feet)
body: Aspen, Colorado has its modern sporty-chic roots in an unlikely melting pot: Long before Prada, Gucci, and Louis Vuitton set up shop there, it’s where Haight refugees and ski-bum dropouts mixed with cowboys, ranchers and, in more recent decades, real estate barons and financial wizards looking for a high-energy second or third home.

More recently, it’s the site of another interesting meeting of the minds: Moncler’s sporty, alpine-inspired performance line, Moncler Grenoble, and Aspen’s historic 19th-century landmark Hotel Jerome, Auberge Collection. Continuing the recent trend of fashion brands expanding from merely selling things to, you know, providing unique experiences —from hotels, restaurants, and cafes to cultural offerings ( Prada Mode and Gucci’s Memoria among them), this new partnership combines a full-spectrum experience at the Jerome with a once-in-a-lifetime hike in the magical terrain surrounding Aspen, led by a guide from the renowned Aspen Center for Environmental Studies (ACES).

articles.summary: With paradisiacal pools, Balinese charm, and seriously great eats, these are the budget-friendly boltholes to consider for your Indonesian escape.
body: Alongside all the mystique and magic swirling around Bali, it’s long been famous as an affordable destination. One where it’s possible to stay in a glorious villa, swim in a stunner of an infinity pool, frolic on picturesque beaches, eat well, and drink all the coconuts one can slurp without spending a small fortune. As I witnessed firsthand while living on the paradisiacal island for four years, affordable hotels in Bali are everywhere, even as prices have undoubtedly risen in recent years. It’s still very possible to have an epic Bali vacation on a budget, especially when selecting a stay that offers a lot for a very reasonable rate.

articles.title: Pixel Watches Are Getting Two New Health Tracking Features
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Google’s “Health Guardian” feature set is rolling out to Pixel Watches 3, 4, and 5 this week, and to Fitbit Air users “later this year.” Google says the new features will include reports on your blood pressure trends and on insulin resistance, which…
body: Insulin resistance is associated with type 2 diabetes, and can be an early sign that you are heading toward pre-diabetes or diabetes. When your body’s insulin receptors stop responding as strongly to insulin, you’re more likely to have higher blood glucose.

Insulin resistance is normally measured with bloodwork. For example, your fasting glucose levels and fasting insulin are combined into a score called HOMA-IR. If you’re concerned about insulin resistance or pre-diabetes, it’s best to talk to an actual healthcare professional to find out what tests they recommend, and what to do with the results.
The insulin resistance feature coming to Google Health is, Google notes, “not intended for medical purposes” and “not a pre-screener for diabetes.”
